issues.description: The problem statement is inconsistent about the type of the Farm.animals collection: the UML diagram (problem_statement.md) defines animals as List<Animal>, while the textual Part 3 explicitly requires using a Set implemented as a HashSet to ensure uniqueness. The provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList). This mismatch between UML, textual instructions, template expectations and the solution can confuse students about which collection type to use and whether duplicates must be prevented.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and templates consistent. Either: (A) Update the UML and textual instructions to require a List (and adjust the text that mentions uniqueness), or (B) update the template and solution to use a Set<Animal> backed by a HashSet (change the animals field, constructor initialization, getter/setter signatures, and addAnimal to use set.add) so the implementation matches the textual requirement of unique animals.

issues.description: The conceptual entity representing the collection of animals in Farm is referenced inconsistently: the UML in the problem statement shows animals: List<Animal>, the textual instructions explicitly require a Set implemented with a HashSet, and the solution implements animals as a List backed by an ArrayList. This mismatch (List vs Set/HashSet) creates confusion for students about which collection type to implement and which behavior (e.g., uniqueness of elements) is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the animals collection consistent across artifacts. Preferably follow the explicit textual requirement and change the solution (and UML if needed) to use a Set: declare private Set<Animal> animals; and initialize it in the no-argument constructor with new HashSet<>(); update getters/setters and iteration accordingly. Alternatively, if List semantics are intended, update the problem text to remove the HashSet/Set requirement and make the UML/text consistently show List/ArrayList.
